---
title: "Feature registry"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

Every SAS function, format and informat that sasonr accepts has a row in one
of two registries, `inst/registry/functions.csv` and
`inst/registry/formats.csv`. The rows are generated by
`tools/update_registry.R` from the offline conformance results — one SAS
9.4 program per case, run by real SAS for the gold standard and by sasonr
offline — and are never edited by hand.

The cases of a function form a matrix: the documented usages, missing and
special missing values, 0, −0, negative, non-integer and extreme numbers,
blank, padded and long (200, 32,767) character values, a value of the other
type (which SAS converts), each modifier or option value, too few and too
many arguments (compile-time errors), the length of the result as a new
variable, `_ERROR_` and the log NOTEs; common functions also run in
`%SYSFUNC` and PROC SQL. Formats and informats are tested at their minimum,
default and maximum widths, with decimals, negative and missing values,
widths too small for the value and invalid input (with `?`/`??`).

Each case is classified as

* **pass** – every compared layer agrees with SAS (data set values bit for
  bit, result length, `_ERROR_`, log NOTEs, PUT output, listing); when SAS
  stops with an ERROR, sasonr must report a SAS ERROR at the same step;
* **approximate** – only numbers differ, in the last bits (typically a
  probability function computed with a different algorithm); this is not a
  pass;
* **unsupported** – sasonr stops with `sasonr_unsupported` (fail loud) where
  SAS ran;
* **mismatch** – any other difference: a value, the display of a value, a
  log NOTE, or sasonr failing loud or stopping with an R error where SAS
  stopped with an ERROR.

Every comparison is exact: numbers bit for bit (IEEE 754 pattern),
character values after removing trailing blanks; there is no tolerance.
A feature is **verified** when all its cases pass; **partial** when some
cases pass and every other case fails loud (the feature runs only inside its
verified domain: a run-time guard makes every other input fail loud in both
modes); **not_comparable** when its value depends on the session clock (only
the type and range are compared); **approximate** when some results differ
from SAS in the last bits; **mismatch** when some case differs in any other
way; **unsupported** when every case fails loud; **unverified** when it has
no case yet. A function also records the contexts in which its cases agree
(`contexts_verified`: DATA step, PROC SQL, `%SYSFUNC`).

The option `sasonr.strict` (default `TRUE`) uses the status at run time:
a program that uses a function, format or informat that is not `verified`,
`partial` or `not_comparable` (or one missing from the registry), or a
function in a context in which it has not been verified (WHERE expressions
have no cases yet), stops with a condition of class `sasonr_not_verified`, a
subclass of `sasonr_unsupported`, that names the feature, its status or
context and the SAS line. PUTN, PUTC, INPUTN and INPUTC check the format they
name at run time. With `options(sasonr.strict = FALSE)` the program runs and
each such feature gives a warning of class `sasonr_unverified`.

The cases of a function or format are one SAS program (one step per case,
inputs listed per case); each case is still compared on its own: the
value bit for bit, type and length, `_ERROR_`, the log NOTEs of its step
(with line numbers) and its PUT output.

Verification is recorded per SAS 9.4 maintenance release (column
`sas_version`): the tables below show the default release, TS1M7.
`options(sasonr.sas_version = "TS1M2")` selects the TS1M2 rows, which come
only from TS1M2 gold (see `?sasonr_sas_version`); a feature without TS1M2
evidence is `unverified` there.

## Functions

```{r}
fn <- utils::read.csv(system.file("registry", "functions.csv", package = "sasonr"),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
fn <- fn[fn$sas_version == "TS1M7", ]
tab <- table(factor(fn$status, c("verified", "partial", "not_comparable", "approximate", "mismatch", "unsupported", "unverified")))
cat(sprintf("Functions: %d (%s); cases: %d, of which %d agree bit for bit.",
            nrow(fn), paste(sprintf("%s %d", names(tab), as.integer(tab)), collapse = ", "),
            sum(fn$cases), sum(fn$pass)))
```

```{r}
knitr::kable(fn[, c("name", "status", "cases", "pass", "approximate", "mismatch", "unsupported",
                    "result_length", "contexts_verified", "note")],
             col.names = c("Function", "Status", "Cases", "Exact", "Approximate", "Other differences", "Fail loud",
                           "Result length", "Verified contexts", "Note"))
```

Besides the matrix, some functions have targeted probes (`fn_probe`: several
hundred random arguments each, one SAS program per probe). A `partial`
function whose differences from SAS are confined to identifiable inputs has
a **verified domain**; a run-time check makes every input outside it fail
loud (`sasonr_unsupported`), in strict mode and outside it:

```{r}
dom <- fn[nzchar(fn$domain %||% ""), c("name", "domain")]
knitr::kable(dom, col.names = c("Function", "Verified domain (other inputs fail loud)"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Formats and informats

```{r}
fm <- utils::read.csv(system.file("registry", "formats.csv", package = "sasonr"),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
fm <- fm[fm$sas_version == "TS1M7", ]
tab <- table(factor(fm$status, c("verified", "partial", "approximate", "mismatch", "unsupported", "unverified")))
cat(sprintf("Formats and informats: %d (%s); cases: %d, of which %d agree bit for bit.",
            nrow(fm), paste(sprintf("%s %d", names(tab), as.integer(tab)), collapse = ", "),
            sum(fm$cases), sum(fm$pass)))
```

```{r}
knitr::kable(fm[, c("name", "kind", "status", "sas_minw", "sas_defw", "sas_maxw", "cases", "pass",
                    "approximate", "mismatch", "unsupported", "note")],
             col.names = c("Name", "Kind", "Status", "Min w", "Default w", "Max w", "Cases", "Exact",
                           "Approximate", "Other differences", "Fail loud", "Note"))
```

Width limits are those SAS 9.4 reports for the format (`dictionary.formats`).

## Procedure statistics

`inst/registry/proc_stats.csv` has one row per procedure and statistic
(and condition, such as a WEIGHT statement), generated by
`tools/update_proc_registry.R` from SAS gold probes: about 1,700 groups of
random size and magnitude, presented sorted, reversed and shuffled, with
missing values, ties and signed zeros. Each statistic is compared bit for
bit with the value SAS writes to the output data set. The status works like
the function status: `approximate` and `unverified` statistics stop the
program in strict mode (condition `sasonr_not_verified` naming the procedure
and the statistic), `partial` statistics run inside their domain and fail
loud outside it.

What the probes showed: sums are plain sequential additions in observation
order (R's `sum()` accumulates in extended precision and differs); PROC SQL
computes its moments from the first value of the group and the shifted sums
with fused multiply-adds; PROC SQL reorders the rows of a group unless the
data set is flagged as sorted by the GROUP BY columns; quantiles interpolate
between neighbours even when the result is one of them.

```{r}
ps <- utils::read.csv(system.file("registry", "proc_stats.csv", package = "sasonr"),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ps <- ps[ps$sas_version == "TS1M7", ]
tab <- table(factor(ps$status, c("verified", "partial", "approximate", "unverified")))
cat(sprintf("Procedure statistics: %d rows (%s).", nrow(ps),
            paste(sprintf("%s %d", names(tab), as.integer(tab)), collapse = ", ")))
```

```{r}
knitr::kable(ps[, c("proc", "statistic", "condition", "status", "compared", "identical", "domain", "note")],
             col.names = c("Procedure", "Statistic", "Condition", "Status", "Values compared",
                           "Bit-identical", "Verified domain", "Note"), row.names = FALSE)
```
